problem:
Let $a, b,$ and $n$ be positive integers with both $a$ and $b$ greater than or equal to $2$ and less than or equal to $2n$. Define an $a \times b$ cell loop in a $2n \times 2n$ grid of cells to be the $2a + 2b - 4$ cells that surround an $(a - 2) \times (b - 2)$ (possibly empty) rectangle of cells in the grid. For example, the following diagram shows a way to partition a $6 \times 6$ grid of cells into $4$ cell loops.

| P   P P   P | Y   Y |
| P | R R | P | Y | Y |
| P | R R | P | Y | Y |
| P   P P   P | Y | Y |
| G   G G   G | Y | Y |
| G   G G   G | Y   Y |

Find the number of ways to partition a $10 \times 10$ grid of cells into $5$ cell loops so that every cell of the grid belongs to exactly one cell loop.
reasoning:
Let the grid size be $N \times N$ with $N=10$. We are looking for the number of ways to partition the $10 \times 10$ grid into 5 cell loops.
Each cell loop is an $a \times b$ rectangle's boundary.
The number of cells in an $a \times b$ loop is $2a + 2b - 4$.
Let the dimensions of the 5 loops be $(a_i, b_i)$ for $i=1, \dots, 5$.
The total number of cells in the grid is $10 \times 10 = 100$.
The total number of cells in the 5 loops is $\sum_{i=1}^5 (2a_i + 2b_i - 4) = 100$.
This simplifies to $\sum_{i=1}^5 (a_i + b_i - 2) = 50$, so $\sum_{i=1}^5 (a_i + b_i) = 50 + 10 = 60$.
